discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies (WMAP), establishing the standard cosmological model and the cosmic abundance of non-baryonic dark matter

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, conceived and led by Bennett with Page as instrument lead and Spergel leading the theoretical interpretation, measured the temperature and polarization anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background with unprecedented precision. Its acoustic-peak measurements fixed the geometry, age and composition of the Universe to percent level, showing that about 85% of matter is non-baryonic dark matter and that the primordial fluctuations are nearly scale-invariant and Gaussian, as inflation predicts. This turned cosmology into a precision science and created the six-parameter LambdaCDM model. For particle physics the impact is direct: the WMAP dark-matter density is the benchmark relic abundance against which every collider and direct-detection search for dark-matter candidates, including supersymmetric neutralinos, is interpreted. WMAP links the smallest and largest structures in nature, and its results have been robustly confirmed by Planck.
